title: P-256: 1024-copy forward loop with unchanged 512-copy backward loop

claims.statement: For uniform full-production P-256 Q=[x]P in the protected target, the cold classical algorithm supplied in proof.md, source-proof.md and predecessor-proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.3900001 under the explicitly retained H1, M1/L-ori, H3 and H-trail premises. Total charged computation is at most 2^126.728594 units at C=1000 scalar AArch64 instructions per unit, including preprocessing, failures, restarts, lookup, transfers, replay, verification and output. Peak memory is below 2^77 bytes, preprocessing at most 2^89.961190 units and advice zero. All source parameters remain fixed, including A=2^32, K=2^32, B=2^28 and tau=0.4943073. Only the forward prefix-loop unroll changes from 512 to 1024 identical bodies. Its lane order and values are identical, while its control saves exactly B/512 instructions per call; the backward loop and rare paths are unchanged. The complete ledger gives log2 work approximately 126.7285939 and conditional success above 0.3900001438. The bound is conditional and analytical, not a production attack or new compiled measurement.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the inherited complete production ledger and reduced-order procedure, plus an independent exact forward-loop order, control-count and branch-range audit.
